meta.topic: Reading: public library cards, borrowing rules, library e-books, book and e-reader prices, and time spent reading
meta.confirmedRule: confirmed:true only when the figure was read from the library's, retailer's, maker's or statistics agency's own page on the read date. confirmed:false means the page blocked the fetch (403, redirect loop, bot check) and the figure comes from a search engine's summary of it, or from a secondary source. Null means not found; never invented.

engineContext.howUnwindIsLoved: LOVED_IN.unwind lists the interests that make an hour to yourself 'loved' (art, design, film, film_history, film_preservation, games, history, music, photography, technology, television, theatre, writing). lovedIn() keeps an interest only if, at home, the person owns the gear GEAR_FOR names for it: tv for film/film_history/film_preservation/television, console for games, speaker for music. Away from home a hotel's or sublet's TV serves. A loved hour gives LOVED_MOOD 1.5x mood and LOVED_RELIEF 1.25x stress relief.
engineContext.readingInterestNote: GENERAL_INTERESTS (interests.ts) has no 'reading', 'books' or 'literature' id as of 2026-10-02; 'writing' and 'history' are the nearest. A reader's hour needing a book would need a new interest id (e.g. 'reading') added to GENERAL_INTERESTS and LOVED_IN.unwind, and a GEAR_FOR-style need satisfied by an owned book, an e-reader, or a library loan that is current (not past its due date). The figures below give the loan periods, item limits and prices that need would run against.

libraries.eligibility: Free to anyone who lives, works, attends school or pays property taxes in New York State. Without a NY State home address, a temporary card is issued that can be upgraded with proof of work/study/property in NY State.
libraries.idRequired: Proof of identity and proof of current home address. Accepted proofs of address include a utility bill, bank or credit card statement, official government letter, or lease/mortgage/rental agreement; out-of-state applicants add proof of NY State work (letter, pay stub) or school (registration, student ID).
libraries.onlineNote: Online application form at nypl.org/library-card/new; in person at any location gives a card immediately.
libraries.note: Eligibility and how-to read from NYPL's own LibAnswers page (confirmed). The detailed proof-of-address list comes from a search summary of nypl.org/help/library-card, which redirect-looped on fetch: treat that list as confirmed:false.

libraries.eligibility: Free for anyone who lives, works, pays property taxes or goes to school in New York State; one card per person.
libraries.idRequired: Full-access card requires a branch visit with 'acceptable ID'.
libraries.onlineNote: An online 'Welcome card'/eCard application exists (bklynlibrary.org/card); full access needs a branch visit.
libraries.note: Eligibility wording (NY State live/work/tax/school, one per person) came from a search summary: confirmed:false for that clause. The ID clause was read on BPL's page.

libraries.eligibility: Valid ID showing name and address may be required. In-state cards are valid 5 years; out-of-state cards 1 year.
libraries.fee: Free to New York State residents
libraries.onlineNote: A 'Get a card' option is referenced but the process was not on the page read.

libraries.eligibility: Library cards are free to residents of California.
libraries.idRequired: Photo ID with name and current address: a California DMV driver's licence or ID card, or a Mexican, Argentinian or Korean consulate ID; or a separate photo ID (passport, school or employee ID, other government photo ID) plus proof of address (printed personal check, credit card statement, rental or property tax receipt, business mail with current postmark). Under-18s need a parent/guardian or adult sponsor signature instead of ID.
libraries.onlineNote: An E-Card application exists at lapl.org/library-card/e-card-application (e-card holders share the 30-item limit).

libraries.eligibility: New Haven residents (adult, teen, child, or e-card). Out-of-town Connecticut residents with a valid hometown library card and photo ID may borrow physical items (not eResources or Cultural Passes). College/university students: card valid for the current academic year; CT-resident students must first hold a hometown card.
libraries.idRequired: Photo ID with current address issued within the past year, or current photo ID plus proof of New Haven address dated within 30 days. Minors need a parent/guardian co-signature.
libraries.onlineNote: Digital card by instant online registration (streaming and e-resources); converted to a physical card in person. Physical cards valid 3 years and usable at any Connecticut public library.
libraries.note: No non-resident purchase fee was stated for people outside Connecticut.

libraries.eligibility: Free if you live, work, go to school or own property in the City of Toronto, or live on a First Nations reserve in Ontario.
libraries.idNote: The page sends applicants to a separate identification-requirements list, not read.
libraries.onlineNote: Only Toronto residents aged 13+ can sign up online, for a Digital Access Card; everyone else registers in person at a branch.

libraries.eligibility: Live or own property in the City of Vancouver; also UBC Endowment Lands, UBC family housing and Musqueam Reserve #2.
libraries.idRequired: ID showing name and current local address; preferred is a BC Driver's Licence or BC Services Card, otherwise two other pieces of ID; newcomers may use a Canadian visa or work permit issued for six months or more plus proof of address.
libraries.onlineNote: A temporary digital card can be registered online (vpl.ca/borrowing/library-card/temporary-digital).
libraries.note: vpl.ca returned 403 to every fetch; all VPL figures are from search summaries. The BC OneCard (www2.gov.bc.ca) lets a cardholder of one BC library borrow at others.

libraries.eligibility: Anyone 16 or over can join free as an adult member; under-16s with parental consent. A free 'guest member' status exists for visitors who cannot prove a permanent address.
libraries.idRequired: Original document (no scans or photos): a utility bill dated in the last six months, driving licence, bank statement or similar.
libraries.onlineNote: Apply online; a MyWestminster Digital Card (16+) can be added to Apple Wallet or Google Pay.

libraries.eligibility: Anyone who lives, works or studies in Dublin City or County, or who already holds a valid public library card from any library service in Ireland.
libraries.idRequired: Photo ID and proof of address (a gas, electricity, telephone or mobile bill, or a bank statement) issued within the past 6 months. Under-18s need parental permission.
libraries.onlineNote: Register online, then visit a branch within one month with photo ID and proof of address to collect the card.

libraries.eligibility: Adults who complete a card application with official ID and proof of address.
libraries.idRequired: Official ID: INE voter card (current), cartilla militar, current passport, cédula profesional, or current Forma FM (immigration form). Proof of address: water, electricity, telephone or gas bill, lease, or constancia domiciliaria (search summary adds: not older than three months).
libraries.onlineNote: Not stated on the page read.
libraries.cardValidity: 2 years; renewal needs original ID and proof of address again; a replacement card is ready 24 hours after request.
libraries.note: The three-month age limit on proof of address came from a search summary (confirmed:false). Forma FM is the old foreigners' document, so a foreign resident can qualify; a tourist without proof of address cannot.
